title: Build peer review sub-agent
description: Create an agent in agents/ that acts as a bar raiser for PR/FAQ drafts. System prompt is adversarial: 'your job is to find weaknesses, not confirm strengths.' Given a .tex draft, it reads critically and returns structured flags: unsupported claims, ambiguous language, judgment calls missing FAQ cross-references, risk ratings that don't match evidence, citation gaps. Does NOT have write access — only generates questions. The main agent evaluates each flag: accept (revise), reject (explain why), or escalate (surface to user). Loop until no critical issues remain.

title: Add ux-bar-raiser.md reference guide
description: Add a reference guide for the UX Bar Raiser lens to skills/prfaq/references/ux-bar-raiser.md. Owns the Usability risk dimension. Should cover the full customer journey, cognitive load of onboarding, mental model alignment, accessibility, error recovery, and the 'would I switch from my current workflow' gut check. Should also sharpen the Customer Quote and Getting Started sections, not just the usability risk rating. Invoked during Phase 3 external FAQs and Phase 2 getting started.

title: /prfaq:feedback-to-us — structured feedback command
description: Build a /prfaq:feedback-to-us slash command that captures structured user feedback (what worked, what didn't, shareability) and transmits it via API call. Builds on /prfaq:rate by adding richer qualitative data collection. Opt-in, clearly labeled, zero document content transmitted. Only build if Phase 1 trials reveal users want to give feedback but the mechanics of /prfaq:rate are too shallow.

title: /prfaq:vote — go/no-go decision framework for PR/FAQ documents
description:
New command that synthesizes the PR/FAQ into a structured go/no-go recommendation. Three decision gates:

1. **Is this a customer problem worth solving?** (value + viability)
   - Does the problem statement hold up under evidence?
   - Is the TAM real and reachable?
   - Do the unit economics work?

2. **Do we have a differentiated solution?** (usability + feasibility)
   - Is the solution meaningfully different from alternatives?
   - Can we actually build it? (technical feasibility, dependencies, timeline)
   - Will customers be able to use it without friction?

3. **Should we do this now?** (opportunity cost / portfolio prioritization)
   - Best use of our resources given what else we could build?
   - Multi-document mode: comparative ranking across a portfolio of PR/FAQs
   - Single-document mode: force an internal FAQ — 'What are the best alternatives for us to pursue if we do not build this?' This ensures teams confront opportunity cost even without multiple PR/FAQs to compare. The answer becomes input to the gate 3 verdict.

Open design questions:
- Input: single prfaq.tex, or multiple .tex files for portfolio comparison
- Output format: structured verdict (GO / CONDITIONAL GO / NO-GO) with evidence trail
- Whether this should read meeting summaries and review reports as additional input (prior deliberation)
- How to weight the three gates — are they all equal, or is gate 1 a hard prerequisite?
- Whether the vote should be an agent (autonomous assessment) or interactive (walks the user through each gate)
- Relationship to /prfaq:meeting — vote is the *decision*, meeting is the *deliberation*

Maps to Cagan's four risks framework (value, usability, feasibility, viability) but reframes around three actionable questions.

title: Auto-save vote output to meetings/ directory
description: The /prfaq:vote command should automatically save its output to ./meetings/vote-YYYY-MM-DD.md after rendering the verdict. Currently the user has to manually ask for this. The command should write the file as part of step 8 or 9, using the same date-stamped naming convention as meeting summaries (meeting-summary-*.md, meeting-hive-summary-*.md). Also move existing meeting summaries from the project root to ./meetings/ (meeting-hive-summary-2026-02-16.md is still in the root).

title: Bug: 'Technical' subsubsection header is a widow in prfaq.pdf
description: The \subsubsection*{Technical} header (line ~276 in prfaq.tex) appears at the bottom of a page without its content. Attempted fixes: nowidow package, needspace in titleformat, explicit needspace before the subsubsection call — none resolved it. The needspace{5\baselineskip} before the header should guarantee 5 lines of space, but LaTeX is still breaking after it. May need to investigate whether adjustwidth inside faqpair environments above it is interfering with the penalty calculation, or use a manual \newpage as a last resort.

title: /prfaq:meeting should persist meeting summaries to file
description: The meeting summary (decisions log, revision queue, research findings) should be automatically saved to a file at the end of the meeting. Suggested path: meeting-summary-YYYY-MM-DD.md in the project root. This ensures the meeting output survives session closure and can be referenced later by /prfaq:feedback. Update meeting-guide.md Phase 3 and the SKILL.md meeting command to include file persistence.
close_reason: Merged PR #1 — meeting summaries auto-persist to meeting-summary-YYYY-MM-DD.md

title: Document version tracking (major.minor revision numbers)
description:
Add version tracking to PR/FAQ output documents so we can see how iteratively people use the product.

The .tex document should carry a version number (e.g. v1.0) that increments:
- Major: significant structural changes (new sections, major rewrites, stage transitions)
- Minor: feedback-driven edits, meeting revisions, research additions

Implementation ideas:
- A \prfaqversion{1}{0} command in the template that renders in the document header/footer
- /prfaq:feedback auto-increments the minor version on each batch or single application
- /prfaq (generation) sets the initial version to 1.0
- Major version bumps could be manual or triggered by stage changes (from prfaq-gt7)
- Version history could be tracked as LaTeX comments or a dedicated section

This is separate from stage (prfaq-gt7) but complementary — stage is about maturity, version is about iteration count.
close_reason: Merged PR #4: \prfaqversion{major}{minor} command, header display, SKILL.md detection, feedback auto-increment

title: Move meeting outputs to ./meetings/ subdirectory
description: Meeting summaries (meeting-summary-*.md, meeting-hive-summary-*.md) currently land in the project root. Move them to ./meetings/ to keep the root clean. Affects: meeting-guide.md (output path), meeting-hive command, SKILL.md (batch mode discovery path for /prfaq:feedback), feedback agent (auto-discover logic), README (output section). Also add meetings/ to the researcher gitignore pattern — these are generated artifacts.

title: Add principal-engineer.md reference guide
description: Add a reference guide for the Principal Engineer lens to skills/prfaq/references/principal-engineer.md. Owns the Feasibility risk dimension. Should cover architecture trade-offs, operational complexity at scale, build vs. buy decisions, dependency risk, data model choices that are hard to reverse, and the 'hardest unsolved technical problem' question. Invoked during Phase 3 technical FAQs.

title: /prfaq:meeting:hive — autonomous consensus meeting via claude-flow
close_reason: Merged PR #6: /prfaq:meeting-hive with claude-flow required, one-way/two-way door framework, Disagree and Commit semantics

title: Add biblatex citation system to template
description: Add biblatex support to the LaTeX template and compile pipeline. The template should use \usepackage[style=authoryear]{biblatex} with a generated .bib file. The compile script needs a biber pass between pdflatex runs. All factual claims in the PR/FAQ should use \cite{key} for real sources (web, research papers, market reports, primary research from ./research/). The skill workflow should instruct the main agent to generate .bib entries as citations are added. The research agent populates these entries.

title: Rename /prfaq:rate to reduce ambiguity with /prfaq:vote
description:
The /prfaq:rate command collects user satisfaction feedback (1-5 rating) about the plugin itself. With /prfaq:vote coming (go/no-go on the PR/FAQ document), 'rate' and 'vote' are too close — users could confuse rating the plugin with rating the document.

Candidates: /prfaq:feedback-to-us, /prfaq:nps, /prfaq:plugin-feedback, /prfaq:satisfaction. Pick one that clearly signals 'tell us about your experience with this tool' vs 'evaluate the document.'

Touches: commands/rate.md (rename file), plugin.json, README.md, SKILL.md, CHANGELOG.md.

title: Researcher agent should cache results in ./research/
description: The prfaq:researcher agent should save its findings (web search results, evidence verdicts, bibliography entries) into ./research/ so subsequent runs don't re-discover the same evidence. Currently each researcher invocation starts from scratch. Saving results would: (1) avoid redundant web searches, (2) build a persistent evidence library across sessions, (3) let users review/curate the raw research. Format TBD — could be markdown summaries, raw search results, or structured JSON.
close_reason: Researcher now persists to ./research/ and checks cached results before web searching

title: /prfaq:streamline — scalpel editor that removes redundancy and imprecision
description: New command and agent that tightens a completed PR/FAQ document by: (1) removing redundancy across FAQs — the document says things once, not twice because they're important, (2) eliminating weasel words, hollow adjectives, and hedge stacking per PRECISE-LLM framework, (3) applying the 'so what' test to every sentence, (4) compressing inflated phrases, (5) cutting throat-clearing and filler. Scalpel, not chainsaw: evidence, citations, customer quotes, risk assessments, numbers, and structural elements are untouchable. Target: 10-20% length reduction with increased focus. Reference: ~/Desktop/PRECISE-LLM.md for banned patterns and required patterns.

title: Add judgment-to-FAQ cross-referencing
description: When the PR/FAQ makes a judgment call (e.g. 'Product X prioritizes A over B to eliminate frustration with C'), it should cross-reference a specific FAQ that explains the reasoning via LaTeX \label/\ref. Each faqpair environment gets an optional \label{faq:slug}. Judgment calls in the press release use 'see FAQ~\ref{faq:slug}' to link to the reasoning. The corresponding FAQ should unpack the judgment: why do we believe this, what evidence supports it, what's the risk if we're wrong. The peer review agent verifies that every judgment call has a corresponding FAQ.

title: /prfaq:externalize — generate a real press release from shipped features
description:
New command that reads the PR/FAQ and CHANGELOG.md (at minimum) to produce an actual external press release reflecting what has shipped. The PR/FAQ is the internal decision artifact; /prfaq:externalize converts it into a customer-facing announcement for a specific release (v1.0, v3.1, etc.).

Inputs:
- prfaq.tex (the full internal document — problem, solution, customer quotes, feature appendix)
- CHANGELOG.md (what actually shipped and when)
- Optional: version argument to target a specific release (default: latest)

Output:
- A press release (.md or .tex) written for external audiences — no internal FAQs, no risk assessment, no feature appendix categories (must do / should do / won't do). Just the news.

Key design decisions:
- How to reconcile the PR/FAQ's aspirational scope with what actually shipped (feature appendix 'Shipped' items + CHANGELOG entries)
- Whether to produce markdown (blog post) or LaTeX (formatted PDF) or both
- How to handle multi-release products (v1 press release vs. v3.1 update announcement — different tone, different structure)
- Whether the agent should rewrite customer quotes to reflect shipped reality or flag stale quotes for user review
- How to handle the case where the PR/FAQ is hypothesis-stage but the user wants to externalize anyway (warning? block? softer language?)

Dependencies: none — can be built independently.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #9: /prfaq:externalize command with release type detection, standalone template, full semver filenames

title: User feedback command (/prfaq:rate) with lightweight telemetry endpoint
description:
Add a /prfaq:rate command that lets users report simple satisfaction feedback: a 1-5 rating for how the tool is performing, plus their document version (from prfaq-5zd). This helps us understand how iteratively people use the product and where quality drops off.

UX:
- /prfaq:rate — prompts for 1-5 rating via AskUserQuestion, optionally reads document version from .tex
- Minimal friction: one question, one click, done
- Optional free-text comment

Backend:
- Need a cheap endpoint to receive ratings. User has a Supabase account — a single Supabase table (ratings: timestamp, version, rating, comment, anonymous_id) with a REST insert would work
- The command POSTs via curl to the Supabase REST API with an anon key
- No PII collected — anonymous_id is a hash of something local (machine ID or random UUID persisted in .claude/prfaq.local.md)
- Endpoint URL and anon key stored in plugin config, not hardcoded

Dependencies:
- Depends on prfaq-5zd (version tracking) for the version field
- Independent of prfaq-gt7 (stage awareness)
close_reason: Merged PR #5: /prfaq:rate command with Supabase telemetry

title: Build research sub-agent
description: Create an agent in agents/ that serves as a research librarian for the main prfaq skill. Interface: given a claim or topic, search for evidence and return structured citations (source, URL/path, summary, relevance). Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, Glob, Read (for ./research/). Returns biblatex-formatted citation entries. Architecture should anticipate MCP server expansion — the agent's prompt stays stable while data source connectors grow (Statista, Google Scholar, SEC/EDGAR, Census/BLS, CRM, product analytics). Each connector would be an MCP server in .mcp.json.
close_reason: Research sub-agent (agents/researcher.md) and /prfaq research command (commands/research.md) created. SKILL.md Phase 0 refactored to invoke researcher agent instead of inline research steps.

title: /prfaq:meeting — simulated review meeting with agentic personas
description:
Add a /prfaq:meeting skill that simulates an Amazon-style PR/FAQ review meeting. The document is reviewed page by page, FAQ by FAQ, with a cast of agentic personalities debating key points.

Architecture:
- **Main Claude is the meeting facilitator.** It orchestrates the flow, synthesizes agent debate, and surfaces decision points to the user as questions.
- **Agent debate is visible.** The user sees the back-and-forth between personas — the thinking, the disagreements, the reasoning. This is valuable context, not noise. The facilitator still synthesizes and asks pointed decision questions, but the user can follow the full conversation and intervene at any point.
- **Agents run in background** (via claude-flow or parallel Task subagents) debating specific sections. Their raw debate output is streamed or presented to the user, then the facilitator distills it into a decision point.
- **The user is the PM and final decision-maker.** They see the debate, then get a clear question like: 'The principal engineer thinks the feasibility risk should be Medium because of the TeX dependency, but the UX bar raiser says the installer mitigates it. Do you want to upgrade feasibility risk, add a mitigation note, or leave it as-is?'

Personas:
- Target customer personas (imagined users with specific contexts — e.g., solo founder, enterprise architect, first-time builder)
- Principal engineer (feasibility lens — from principal-engineer.md)
- Unit economics reviewer (viability lens — from unit-economics.md)
- UX bar raiser (usability lens — from ux-bar-raiser.md)
- Skeptical executive / devil's advocate (value lens — challenges assumptions)

Meeting flow:
1. Facilitator opens the meeting, introduces the document and the cast
2. Walk through section by section (or focus on highest-risk areas first)
3. For each section: agents debate (visible to user), facilitator synthesizes, asks the user a pointed question
4. User decides, facilitator records the decision
5. At the end: summary of decisions made, action items, and agreed changes — optionally feeds into /prfaq:feedback for automated iteration

Key design questions:
- Could use claude-flow for genuine multi-agent parallel debate, or parallel Task subagents with different system prompts
- How to stream/present agent debate so it's readable (threaded? labeled by persona? collapsible?)
- How to make persona voices genuinely distinct (not just the same LLM with different hats)?
- Meeting should be interruptible — user can pause, ask clarifying questions, overrule, or skip sections
- Output format: decisions log, action items, optional automated redraft via /prfaq:feedback

This is the most ambitious feature in the roadmap. It turns a static document review into an interactive decision-making session where you see the thinking, not just the conclusions.
close_reason: V1 complete: 4 persona agents, meeting guide, command, SKILL.md integration, prototype validated

title: /prfaq data tables — structured data appendices for financial models, customer data, metrics
description:
When the PR/FAQ has solid financial models, customer data tables, survey results, or usage metrics, these should be presentable as structured appendices in the compiled PDF — not just prose summaries buried in FAQ answers.

Open design questions:
- New agent vs. researcher extension vs. compile-time feature
- LaTeX table environments needed (the template currently has no table support beyond basic tabular)
- How to source the data: inline from the user, from ./research/ files, from quarry-mcp, from CSV/spreadsheet imports
- Which appendix types matter most: unit economics tables, TAM build-up, customer interview summary matrices, feature comparison grids, survey result tables
- Whether data tables should be cross-referenceable from FAQ answers (like featureref/faqref)

This is a P3 — useful but not blocking any current workflow. The current approach of describing data in prose works; tables would make it more rigorous and scannable for executive review.

title: Add unit-economics.md reference guide
description: Add a reference guide for unit economics to skills/prfaq/references/unit-economics.md. Owns the Viability risk dimension. Should cover CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC ratio, payback period, gross margin, contribution margin. Help distinguish products where unit economics matter (SaaS, marketplace) from ones where they don't (open source, internal tools).

title: /prfaq:feedback — directed iteration from pointed user feedback
description:
Add a /prfaq:feedback skill that takes specific user feedback (e.g., '/prfaq:feedback the adoption risk should be more from the perspective of enterprise procurement') and drives a full iteration cycle: interpret the feedback, redraft affected sections, then run peer review to validate the changes. This closes the loop between 'I see a problem' and 'the document is better' without the user having to manually locate sections, rewrite LaTeX, or remember to re-run review.

Key design questions:
- Should feedback target specific sections (risk assessment, customer quote, problem statement) or let the skill infer scope from the feedback text?
- How much should it redraft before asking the user to confirm vs. presenting options?
- Should it automatically invoke peer-reviewer after redraft, or ask first?
- Should it support multiple feedback items in one invocation (bulleted list)?

The skill should read the current prfaq.tex, interpret the feedback against the document context, make targeted edits, recompile, and optionally run peer review on the changes.

title: Explore versioned/staged PR/FAQ documents
description:
The tool needs to understand what stage a product is at so meetings, peer reviews, and generation prompts are calibrated appropriately. A pre-prototype PR/FAQ (hypothesis stage, no users) should be evaluated differently than a PR/FAQ for a new feature on an existing product with rich customer data.

Stage affects: (1) what evidence the peer reviewer expects, (2) how aggressively meeting personas critique missing data, (3) what questions the generation workflow asks, (4) what the reviewer considers 'good enough' for the current stage.

Design constraints:
- Must not complicate every prompt — the current system works well
- Lightweight concept: a stage marker in the .tex document (e.g. a LaTeX command or environment variable) that skill prompts can read and branch on
- Suggested stages: Hypothesis (pre-validation), Validated (post-interviews/testing), Growth (existing product, rich data)
- Each stage sets expectations, not gates — you can still write a Hypothesis-stage doc with strong evidence

Implementation approach: add a \prfaqstage{} command to the template, teach the skill prompts to read it and adjust their bar. Reference guides may need a small 'stage calibration' section.
close_reason: Merged PR #3: stage awareness via \prfaqstage{} command

title: Test meeting flow on dogfood prfaq.tex
close_reason: Prototype passes all 4 criteria: distinct voices, substantive disagreement, structural constraints work, synthesizable responses

title: Support quarry-mcp as optional research data source
description:
Add optional integration with quarry-mcp (https://github.com/jmf-pobox/quarry-mcp) as a data source for the research sub-agent. Quarry provides semantic search over the user's entire local file corpus — PDFs, images, notes, source code, scanned documents — via MCP.

This replaces the need to cherry-pick files into ./research/. Instead, the research agent can query 'customer interviews about onboarding friction' or 'market sizing for developer tools' and get relevant chunks from anywhere the user has indexed.

Implementation:
- Add quarry as an optional MCP server in the plugin's .mcp.json (or document how users add it)
- The research agent checks if quarry tools (search_documents, get_page) are available. If yes, use them as a primary search source alongside WebSearch and ./research/ files.
- If quarry is not installed, fall back gracefully to current behavior (./research/ scan + web search)
- The research agent should use quarry's collection filtering if the user has organized documents into collections (e.g., a 'research' or 'interviews' collection)
- Citations from quarry results should include the source file path and page/chunk reference

This is the first third-party data source connector for the research agent, establishing the pattern for future integrations (Statista, EDGAR, Google Scholar, etc.).
close_reason: Researcher agent updated with specific quarry search_documents tool usage (parameters, collection filtering, citation metadata). README documents quarry-mcp as optional prerequisite. No plugin-level MCP config needed — quarry install registers globally.

title: /prfaq:import — ingest user-written PR/FAQ for research, feedback, and formatting
description:
Add a /prfaq:import skill that accepts an existing user-written PR/FAQ document (plain text, markdown, Google Doc paste, or raw .tex) and runs it through the full prfaq pipeline for enrichment:

1. **Parse and structure**: Read the user's document, map it to the PR/FAQ template structure (headline, problem, solution, customer quote, FAQs, risk assessment, feature appendix). Identify missing sections.

2. **Research**: Invoke the researcher agent to find evidence for claims made in the document. Generate .bib entries for unsupported assertions. Surface contradicting evidence.

3. **Feedback**: Run peer review against the full reference guide suite (decision quality, four risks, common mistakes, pr-structure, faq-structure, unit economics, principal engineer, UX bar raiser). Identify cognitive biases, ambiguous language, risk rating mismatches.

4. **Formatting**: Convert the content into the prfaq LaTeX template with proper environments (faqpair, customerquote, spokespersonquote), citation cross-references (\cite{}, \faqref{}), and professional typesetting. Compile to PDF.

5. **Gap analysis**: Present what's missing — required FAQs not addressed, risk dimensions not evaluated, Won't Do list absent, etc. Offer to fill gaps interactively.

This feature makes the plugin useful to people who already have a PR/FAQ draft (from a workshop, a Google Doc, or their own process) and want to upgrade it with evidence, structure, and professional output. It's the on-ramp for users who don't start from scratch.

Key design questions:
- Input formats: plain text paste, markdown file, .tex file, URL to a Google Doc?
- How much should it restructure vs. preserve the user's original voice and organization?
- Should it ask permission before adding/changing sections, or present a full proposed restructure?
- How to handle a document that's fundamentally not a PR/FAQ (e.g., a pitch deck outline, a product brief)?
close_reason: Implemented /prfaq:import command — 10-step pipeline for converting existing documents to PR/FAQ format

title: /prfaq:feedback batch mode for meeting revision queues
description: After a /prfaq:meeting with multiple REVISE decisions, the user currently needs to run /prfaq:feedback N times (once per directive). This is cumbersome. Options to explore: (1) /prfaq:feedback --meeting that reads the meeting summary file and applies all directives sequentially, (2) /prfaq:feedback --batch that accepts multiple directives in one invocation, (3) a new /prfaq:meeting-apply command. Key challenge: each directive may cascade, so later directives need to operate on already-revised text. Sequential application with recompile between each is likely correct but slow.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #2. /prfaq:feedback now auto-discovers meeting summaries and applies all directives sequentially.
